I was trying to share our story of how our company went from nothing over a one year period and got removed for spamming. I use reddit occasionally but was given a link by a government agency that told a story of a fellow Indie Game Designer and his experiences. I found the article very helpful, but wanted to add a few more points of how we did our process for the Indie Game Devs and lovers alike. Here is the article below and would love to hear some comments or thoughts. I did not even post our website in the article.

Two guys built a company and took the worst game idea and turned it into a HUGE success.

I started a company last year after my buddy and I wanted to make a few games as a hobby. This hobby escalated as a business quickly after getting some analytics and reviews of our pilot game Quick Wordz. One of my friends even got hired on at Zynga as a result of the game and level design I had done.

After Quick Wordz picked up a lot of interest I decided to make another word game that had more promise and addictive nature. This game is called Alpha Quest and was a finalist at the Canadian Video Game Awards in Dec 2015 before it launched. We caught the interest of a publisher MOVYL Entertainment who launched the game last month on our behalf. With these wheels in motion we launched a game as an alpha on the app store called Tappy Toes.

It started out as game of continuously tapping an egg until you reached a high score. It got a lot of people laughing and having fun with its cute graphics. Once we seen we had some potential here as it was a game easily described as a hybrid of Flappy Bird and Mr. Jump and had similar addictive properties. The graphics are amazing, the sounds real and funny with some hilarious customization like the ability to change to a tattooed leg and rubber boot.

We recently launched the beta of Tappy Toes on iOS with all new game play, style, sounds, graphics and level design.

So the formula we used is:

1 Do research and a lot of it to make sure your game idea is not out there. Being original is far better than a cloner. Even if there is a game close to your idea you still have a chance to make a different game so don't get discouraged. 

2 Once you have the idea do the coding yourself like us, hire good quality programmers or at least reach out to a company and see if they are willing to partner with you. Get an NDA for sure with a reputable lawyer or ask a gaming company to provide one to you. I don't mind sharing our company one to developers who might not be able to afford a lawyer. 

3 Build a prototype and test it with a group of testers from a website like Beta Family and get some feedback on UI and retention. Yes use analytics sdk on your game it is imperative and don't forget to ask questions on forums and don't be afraid of rejection or a lack of response as there is about a 1/20 chance of having people reply. 

4 After the prototype and testing phase you need to look at publishers and marketing of your game. Not everyone will have good things to say about it. You will know if it is addictive based on the analytics. I am also willing to work with Indie Developers that are not familiar with them.

5 At least a month before you publish the game you need to market it to the press. Email video bloggers, constantly tweet and Facebook to friends to build the hype. Make a marketing budget and use FB ads and marketing firms. Stay away from google adwords and ad campaign companies that charge for installs as that for an indie company is way to expensive at this point. 

6 If you at least use somewhat of a process like this you will be on track and again this worked for us and may vary for each situation, game genre, and budget.
